## 6. Function

Implement exactly this behaviour (from the reference program's documentation):

```text
Writes the tracking test's input: a monochrome (256-level
  grey) animated GIF that looks like black-and-white street video of a
  pedestrian walking along a pavement, 128 x 96 pixels (4:3), 50 frames
  of 100 ms = 5 seconds, looping.
  The scene is rendered with 4 x 4 supersampling (anti-aliased edges) and
  lit from the upper left: an overcast sky with soft clouds, stone and
  brick facades with recessed windows, cornices and shop fronts, a tree,
  a street lamp, pavement slabs in perspective with a kerb and a strip of
  road. The pedestrian (dark coat and trousers, lighter face and hands,
  an 8-frame walk cycle with bending knees and swinging arms, each limb
  shaded) casts a soft shadow on the pavement. Camera effects: lens
  vignetting, a gentle tone curve, film grain that changes every frame
  and a few dust specks.
  Every background tone stays above the tracking threshold (luma 80):
  the pedestrian's dark clothing is the only dark object, as in a
  photograph of someone in a dark coat on a bright street; the dust
  specks are single pixels (the tracker's run filter ignores them).
  Pure Python (own LZW encoder), no packages needed.
  The true box of the figure in every frame is written next to the GIF
  (<name>.truth.txt: frame x0 y0 x1 y1, pixels at least half covered)
  for reference; the testbench measures its own truth from the frames.
```

Per function:

```text
lzw_encode: GIF LZW of a list of colour indices -> bytes (code stream, before sub-blocking).

write_gif: frames: lists of W*H grey levels 0-255; global palette of 256 greys, loops forever.

vnoise: Smooth value noise, about -0.5 .. 0.5.

street: Grey level (0..255, before the camera) of the street at sub-pixel (x, y).

tree: Tree in front of the buildings at x ~ 104: grey level or None.

lamp: Street lamp at x ~ 44 (painted iron, mid grey).

figure: Body parts of the walker (feet on GROUND, centre column cx, phase 0..1 of the walk cycle),
back to front: ((a, b), radius at a, radius at b, lit tone, shaded tone).

body_tone: Grey of the front-most part covering (x, y), shaded with light from the left, or None.

in_shadow: The walker's shadow on the pavement: the figure laid down towards the lower right.

render_figure: Composites the walker and its shadow over img; returns the figure's box (pixels at least
half covered).

camera: Vignetting, a soft tone curve (brighter highlights), film grain and dust -> 8 bits.
```

## 6a. Industry reference check

Comparison of section 6 with published engineering references. Every difference is a `TODO(REF-...)` written as a prompt for updating the program.

```text
// Industry reference check - make_pedestrian_gif.py (2026-10-16)
// Sources:
//   [1] CompuServe, "Graphics Interchange Format Version 89a" (1990),
//   https://www.nayuki.io/page/gif89a-specification-html (LZW minimum code size, clear = 2^min,
//   EOI = clear + 1, code width grows when the next code reaches 2^width, 12-bit maximum,
//   255-byte sub-blocks, graphic control extension); LZW walkthrough
//   https://giflib.sourceforge.net/whatsinagif/lzw_image_data.html; NETSCAPE2.0 loop extension
//   (de facto)
//   [2] K. Perlin, "An image synthesizer", SIGGRAPH 1985; F. K. Musgrave in Ebert et al.,
//   "Texturing and Modeling: A Procedural Approach" (fBm = sum of octaves, frequency x
//   lacunarity, amplitude x gain); https://thebookofshaders.com/13/
// Published algorithm / rules:
//   GIF89a: header, logical screen with global colour table, LZW image data (minimum code size
//   8 for 256 colours, clear / EOI codes, width growth, 12-bit limit, clear when full),
//   255-byte sub-blocks, graphic control extension per frame, trailer 0x3B. Textures: value
//   noise summed over octaves (fBm).
// Comparison with this program (section 6):
//   Matches: LZW codes and width growth as in the spec, clear when the table is full, sub-
//   blocks, GCE with disposal 1, NETSCAPE2.0 looping (a de facto extension, not part of
//   GIF89a), fBm textures.
// Result: in line with the reference; no TODO.
```
